verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev positions itself as a platform to "build AI agents and workflows in TypeScript." `chat.agent` runs each conversation as a durable, long-lived task. Prompt templates can be defined as code and versioned, and a `needsApproval: true` flag pauses a run for human approval, which suggests gated tool calls inside agent runs. Because tasks are plain async functions, LLM steps can sit inside ordinary workflows, and a community user reports running an AI automation platform on it. missing for 10: explicit documentation of model/provider choice, detailed tool-use (function-calling) docs beyond the approval snippet, independent hands-on corroboration of agent steps with tools.
